docs.text: Welcome! Welcome to the central knowledge repository for the international Community for Artificial Intelligence in Multiple Sclerosis . This wiki brings together researchers, clinicians, data scientists, software engineers, and patient advocates worldwide to accelerate AI-driven advancements in MS research, diagnosis, treatment, and care. What to Expect This wiki serves as an open-access, community-maintained knowledge hub. Here is what you will find inside: Guides & Tutorials: Step-by-step walkthroughs Domain Glossaries: Definitions on MS- and AI-related topics Datasets & Benchmarks: Index of open-access MS datasets, tools, etc State of the Art (SOTA) Summaries: High-level summaries of landmark papers at the intersection of AI and MS. Best Practices & Ethics: Guidelines for data privacy, algorithmic bias reduction, and safe clinical translation How to Contribute We welcome contributions from everyone—whether you are writing code, explaining a clinical concept, or fixing typos! 1. Contribution Workflow Explore Existing Content: Check existing pages to see where your expertise fits best. Open an Issue / Pitch an Update: For major additions or structural updates, open a GitHub Issue first to discuss your idea with community maintainers. Fork & Branch: Create a feature branch off of main (e.g., feature/add-mri-segmentation-tutorial ). Submit a Pull Request (PR): Fill out our PR template detailing your changes and link any relevant issues. 2. Ways You Can Help ✍️ Write Content: Draft tutorials, summarize recent literature, or expand clinical/technical glossary terms. 🔍 Review Content: Peer-review pending PRs for clinical accuracy or technical correctness. 🌐 Localization & Accessibility: Help translate pages or improve accessibility for non-native readers. 🛠️ Maintain Infrastructure: Improve search indexing, fix broken links, or refine wiki navigation. Content Guidelines To maintain quality and clarity across diverse disciplines: * Target Clear Communication: Remember our audience spans both clinical and technical backgrounds. Define complex terms or link to the internal Glossary. * Cite Sources: Always cite peer-reviewed research, public datasets, or official guidelines when introducing scientific facts. * Maintain Privacy: Never upload, commit, or link to patient data or proprietary/restricted clinical records. Code of Conduct We are committed to fostering a welcoming, inclusive, and collaborative environment. Please review our Code of Conduct prior to contributing. Connect with Us Website: iaims.org Discussions & Community Forum: Check our Discord Issues & Suggestions: Open an Issue
